patterns.property: purpose distractor verb: ask/say/describe/compare/name/complain/claim/argue/promise/prove/date is never the key
patterns.evidence: 13 of 20 purpose items carry at least one option opening with one of these verbs (28 options); none is the key. Keys open show/explain/give a reason/help picture/point out/raise/question/offer. E.g. I-D2-1 'To ask the woman to carry a heavy bag', 'To promise that the ankle will be fine'; A-C-4 'To complain that the plan takes too much effort'; B-L-2 'To claim that snails ruin...', 'To argue that snails should be studied...'. show (7/18) and explain (3/17) are mixed.

patterns.property: purpose key states the obstacle / reason against (negation or limiting word)
patterns.evidence: Of the 7 purpose items where any option has not/no/nobody/can't/bad/against/little, the key carries it in 6: A-C-4 'Thursday after school is a bad time', B-L-2 'why nobody could count them all', C-L-1 'had no training in science', F-C-1 'a reason against her idea', I-D2-1 'a reason for not walking home'. Only exception A-L-3 (distractor 'animals that need little sleep').

patterns.property: modal/hedge (may, might, could, likely/unlikely, played a part) on the key
patterns.scope: batch (concentrated in kind purpose 4/4 and Part 3 inference)
patterns.evidence: Key has it in 9/11; purpose 4/4 (D-C-3 'a spray could ruin that day's number', F-L-5 'a better way the town could help', I-L-2 'could be useful'); E-C-3 key 'It's unlikely to change the council's vote'; G-L-2 key 'They may explain why the black spots appeared'. Exceptions D-C-2, F-L-4 (distractor only). Several hits are ability-'could', so partly lexical; weak.

patterns.property: option stating the first request/plan that the dialogue blocks is never the key
patterns.scope: part 1 + intent-next (and the two Part 2 intent items)
patterns.evidence: Dialogue recipe 'X proposes, Y blocks with a reason, an alternative is adopted' in most Part 1 scripts; the blocked plan is offered as an option 16 times and never keyed, keys are the substitute that keeps the goal: E-D1-1 key 'Take a table inside that still looks over the river' vs 'Sit outside on the balcony'; D-D2-1 key 'Use an exercise machine' vs 'Run laps on the outdoor track'; I-D1-1 key 'Copy two of the pictures with a library machine' vs 'Take the skeleton book home'; G-D2-1 'Find room for the violin in the cabin' not key. Scripts where the first plan wins (F-D4 cakes, E-D3 repair) are never asked about the outcome. All 13 intent-next keys = the adopted alternative.

patterns.property: Part 2: the young/proposing speaker is never simply overruled; options where the older speaker's objection prevails are never the key
patterns.evidence: All 9 conversations end in agreement, compromise, a vote or a shared deferral, and in 6 the student pre-answers the adult's objection ('you've really done your homework', 'more careful than I expected', 'you've convinced me'). Never keyed: B-C-3 'Being persuaded to keep the bird migration poster', D-C-1 'How the man persuades the student to use the window ledge', H-C-2 'A coach refuses a student's request', I-C-4 'Why the woman should give up rowing'. Main-idea twins resolve the same way: the joint/compromise/deferred outcome beats 'one side wins outright' 4/4 (C-C-3 'decide later' vs 'agrees at last'; E-C-4 'club will vote' vs 'choosing the letter'; G-C-2 'lend' vs sell/give for good; I-C-4). Partial exception: F-C-1 key 'To give a reason against her idea' (purpose item; her idea is rejected but the agreed plan uses her counter-proposal).

patterns.property: main-idea: a single-moment detail option is never the key; the key names the whole topic or the resolution
patterns.evidence: Every main-idea item carries 1-3 narrow-detail options (none keyed). In 6 (A-C-1, B-L-5, D-L-6, E-L-3, F-C-2, G-L-5) the key is the ONLY whole-talk option, so it is pickable unheard: B-L-5 key 'How a way of estimating animal numbers works, and its limits' vs 'How heavy rain can wear the paint dots off'. The other 11 include a whole-talk twin (parallel frames in A-L-4, C-L-5, G-C-2, H-C-2, H-L-4), which blocks the tell. Inherent to the kind, but the 6 unique-general items are free.

patterns.property: Part 3 inference/main-idea: the evidence-overclaim option (proves, exact, at once, only possible cause, could never, erases nearly every, does no harm) is never the key
patterns.evidence: Speakers hedge (B, E, G end on open questions) and keys follow: E-L-4 key 'could reveal whether...' vs 'already prove that the railway explanation is the correct one'; G-L-2 key 'may explain' vs 'Scientists see them as the only possible cause'; D-L-5 key 'shakes loose only a little rock' vs 'can split a cliff open at once'; B-L-6 'It would be exact'. Lexical absolutes overall are mixed (5/17), the tell is the certainty-about-evidence claim.

patterns.property: attitude: the dismissive judgement is never the key; key is the favourable one
patterns.evidence: Dismissive options ('too small to be useful', 'will be disproved', 'disappointing up close', 'too simple to be much use', 'Doubtful', 'a poor aim', 'relied more on luck') appear in 7 of 8 attitude items, none keyed. Key is the most favourable option in 6/8 (G-L-4 'better than expected', I-C-1 'better than any the man made', D-L-4 'Confident'); exceptions B-L-4 (target criticised) and F-L-4 ('worthy aim, wrong method' beats 'served well by the rule'). Comparative 'than' frame on key in attitude 4/5 (G-L-4, I-C-1 unique), weak.

checked_clean: key longest by characters: 33/126 (uniquely 27), shortest 30/126 (uniquely 27); per author 3-5 of 14; per kind mixed except relationship 3/5 longest (n=5)
transcript-word overlap: key uniquely highest 42/124 (~34% vs 25%), lowest 34/124; per author 3/14 to 7/14 - mild, not a tell

prompt-word echo: option uniquely echoing the prompt is the key 2/19 (11%) - near-eliminate (prompt-echo distractor recipe, e.g. E-L-5 'when the weekly market first began', F-L-5 'how the town spent its money'), but not 0%
than/rather comparative: 11/25 batch; inference 7/13; detail 0/6 (n small)
numbers in options: 16/39; detail number items use parallel 'About N' sets (G-C-1, I-L-4, B-L-1)
negation batch-wide: 9/23 (only purpose concentrates it, see pattern)
first word/frame: main-idea and lecture options share frames (How/Why/'A way of keeping food...'/'Agreeing...'); purpose all 'To'; no frame unique to keys except verb lists above
speaker favoured in Part 1 keys: last speaker vs first speaker mixed; service worker's suggestion adopted in most scripts but rejected in C-D4, D-D3, E-D3, F-D3

lecture keys = speaker's view/conclusion: inherent to main-idea/attitude; common-belief direction varies (belief confirmed A, H; rejected B, C, F), so 'misconception option never key' not testable as a rule
identical key wording across scripts: none found; A-C and I-C both biology-test study plans and D-L-1/H-L-2 both keyed 'To help ... picture how' (n=2)
